title: Seven days of mantras
lede: A practical, inclusive and carefully labelled spiritual reference, arranged by the seven planetary days: mantras, prayers and verses, each with its text, a readable pronunciation, its meaning and how it can be used.

how.title: How to use this library
paras: The library is organised by the seven planetary weekdays. Each day begins with its planetary symbolism across the shared Western and Indian weekday systems, then offers mantras and prayers arranged by intention. A mantra may be practised on any day; its place here means that its themes complement the day’s symbolism, or that it appeared under that day in Sarvakali’s own list.

The planetary correspondences are traditional astrological symbolism, not a claim that a planet physically changes the atmosphere or determines how every person will feel. A person’s birth chart, circumstances and lived experience are individual.

The pronunciation is a practical reading guide, not a replacement for learning Sanskrit sounds from a knowledgeable teacher. AUM is used throughout; some texts print the opening syllable as Om. The spelling is standardised to AUM without changing the sacred syllable.

Repetition counts are optional. One careful recitation can be more meaningful than a large number repeated mechanically. Where a mantra contains seed syllables (bija), tantric elements or lineage-sensitive material, the library says so. Do not assume every mantra is appropriate for every practitioner.

For traditions outside Hindu Sanskrit mantra practice, the library does not manufacture Sanskrit-style mantras. It uses a documented prayer, hymn, chant or traditional invocation where one can be identified; where no widely attested public formula has been verified, it says so plainly.

rhythm.title: A simple rhythm
rhythm.text: One opening prayer, one main mantra or verse, and one closing intention. You do not need to chant every item listed for a day: choose the practice that genuinely fits your intention and tradition.

labels.title: What the labels mean
labels.openText: A devotional prayer or verse anyone may recite.
labels.guidanceText: Seed syllables, tantric or lineage-held: learn its sounds and use from a qualified teacher. The text is shown for study.
labels.variantText: Shown as supplied for the library; it has not been matched to a published source, so hold it lightly.
labels.verifyText: The wording in the source list could not be matched to a published text, so it is held back until Sarvakali confirms it. Its meaning is given.
labels.draftedText: Purpose and use written for this library, to be approved by Sarvakali.

searchHint: A name, a word of the meaning, a deity or an intention
include: Include mantras to learn with guidance
none: Nothing matches. Try fewer words, or another day.

mantra.supports: What it can support in reflection
mantra.supplied: As supplied in the source list

mantra.doneChant: Complete. It is in your practice for today.

care: Some of these prayers touch grief, illness and fear. They are spiritual practice, never a replacement for medical or psychological care. If you are struggling, please also reach out to a doctor or counsellor; in India, Tele-MANAS is free on 14416, day and night.
